question.text: The minimum possible distance between the points <math><mi>A</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi></mi><mi>a</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>D</mi></math> units, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is

solution.text:
Given points lie on the line y=x-1 and the parabola y=x2+x+1
Thus, the minimum distance occurs along the common normal
∴ At B, dydx=1

or 2x+1=1
⇒x=0
∴B is 0,1
Hence, the shortest distance is D=0-1-12=2 units
